newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks end higher in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks end higher in sluggish trade.

text.p: Indian shares edged higher in lacklustre trade on Monday, as blue-chips posted small gains, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange rose 13.86 points or 0.43 percent to 3,264.52, off the day's highest mark of 3,314.05.
Traders said the market saw little action during the day's trade with attention focussed on pivotal counters.
"People are generally cautious. Confidence is not building up in a big way," said Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive at Lloyds Finance, a Bombay-based brokerage firm
Buying by foreign funds was limited to select stocks, even as the market trend was distinctly sluggish, market players said.
"The market is in range-bound trade. There has demand for blue-chips, but foreign institutions are not agressive buyers," said dealer Sanjeev Choithani at Pashupati Advani.
Market participants said one million shares of state-run petroleum firm, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) changed hands in off-market deals at the National Stock Exchange.
The NSE index lost 1.06 points or 0.11 percent to end at 935.89.
The BPCL deal was struck between a leading domestic institution and a U S based fund which bought the shares at about 287 rupees, market sources said.
Such deals are not reported in trading volumes at exchanges. BPCL shares closed 1.55 rupees higher at 280.55 on the NSE.
The Delhi index rose 5.28 points to 743.25.

At the BSE, SBI rose 1.50 rupees to 231.50, TISCO 1.75 to 191.50, Reliance 1.25 to 212.0 and TELCO 8.25 to 433.25. Hind Lever lost 3.0 to 811.0, Gujarat Ambuja 15.20 to 261.75, Ranbaxy Lab 4.50 to 629.50 and IPCL 0.50 to 116.75.
